skill: Rewrite a reducible first-order linear ODE in the syntactic standard form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x), by collecting terms, canceling permitted factors, and normalizing the derivative coefficient.
learner_operation: Inspect the given equation and each option; identify an algebraically equivalent equation with unit derivative coefficient, all y terms on the left, and y-independent right side. Standard-form recognition alone is insufficient when several options share that form.
reasoning_steps: Expand a square only in the hard family; cancel a common y factor only under y != 0.
Move y terms to the left and independent terms to the right.
Divide all terms by the derivative coefficient on intervals where it is nonzero.
Simplify rational, exponential or trigonometric coefficients and identify P and Q.
Select the unique equivalent standard-form equation from a five-option radio bank.
response_contract: One radio selection from five math choices; canonical example is worked only. The first source has two captured banks, one missing a correct pointer; both encode the same correct equation. Preserve complete banks, allowing UI notation normalization.
difficulty: Eight easy questions cover collection, division, trig simplification and cancellation under y != 0. The square-expansion family is explicitly hard and should not enter an easy delivery.
invariants: First derivative only; no solving or integration.
Unit derivative coefficient in the answer, P and Q depend on x only.
Algebraic equivalence on the stated/original equation domain.
Exactly one keyed standard-form answer; algebraically equivalent nonstandard forms remain distractors.
permitted_variations: Change small signed coefficients, preserving valid distinct distractors and comparable algebra.
Change forcing-term signs or sides and coefficient roles so normalization must be recomputed.
Vary sin/cos within justified same-identity families; vary modest exponential rates and rational coefficients.
Shuffle answer positions; do not fix the correct structural signature when several standard-form options should demand algebra.
Keep target standard form fixed because it defines the knowledge point; this does not justify fixed signs or numerical answers.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: coefficient, sign and supported function assignments
coefficient and sign independent of P where method permits

Lesson states nonidentically-zero a suffices for division; mathematically restrict to intervals where a != 0.

source_case_summary.prompt:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=1-4y\operatorname{sin}⁡x
$$

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2x-y}{x}\,.
$$

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
{e}^{2x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2{e}^{x}y-x=0
$$

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\,y=0
$$

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
y\frac{dy}{dx}+{x}^{2}y={y}^{2}x\,,\,y\ne 0\,.
$$

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+{y}^{2}{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{2}={(1-y\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}^{2}\,.
$$

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\left(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{x+y}{x}\,.
$$

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
5{y}^{2}-y{e}^{-x}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=y,\,y\ne 0.
$$

Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=0\,.
$$
